After putting in 1,000 hours into the other great ARPG, Path of Exile, I decided to give Grim Dawn and try and I have to say, this game is a masterpiece. It has the depth and replayability of Path of Exile without any of the MMO aspects that game has, meaning this game is great for those like myself who enjoy playing a single player game rather than an interconnected one. Pros and Cons I'll list below, but overall Grim Dawn is a 10/10 thanks to its excellent game design and replayability and its unique ARPG world that stands on its own.

Pros =
1. Addictive game design and gameplay loop
2. Incredible build variety (over 30 different class combos with each one playable in multiple ways)
3. Deep character development and customization
4. Unique and interesting world with great lore and soundtrack
5. Fun as hell to play

Cons -
1. Requires a good amount of farming to get best gear (which is normal in ARPG's)
2. A few movement bugs and glitches

Overall Grim Dawn is a must play if you are a fan of ARPG's and a great game to play if you ever wanted to try to Genre. This is easily one of the best ARPG's ever made and I could honestly write an essay on why this game is so good.

Used to love the game but the devs have changed it massively with the latest DLC. Now, many bosses have one-shot attacks and bloated hitpoints to boot. Having to spam dodge sucks. I have been on the ride with GD all the way back to the Kickstarter because it was made in the vein of the oldschool ARPG greats like Diablo 2 and Titan Quest. Now, they seem to be chasing after PoE and that makes me weary of what Grim Dawn 2 will look like. For now, I'll wait and hope that they will revert the balance changes. The game is too tedious to be enjoyable like it once was.

Great sound plus great graphics for the type of game it is plus tight, simple combat = a win. If you like Diablo, Torchlight or something of the sort well this is for you. This game also has good sounding NPCs and even though all of them do not have audio feedback they are all still interesting enough. Also if you like loot this game has it and much more. Another simple thing I like is that the help selection actually works well unlike in other games. It pops open and everything you need to know or much of it is all just set out their for you. Honestly I can't say enough good things about this game. From the skill trees to the regular abilities everything is easy to get to and use. Just get the darn game.

very good game overall

ps. in case you ever get bored with vanilla game, just slap a 'grimarillion' mod on it and sink another couple hundred hours into it

Sometime ago I promised a review to the dev, so now I'm going to correct that mistake.

Grim Dawn is a great action RPG title from the ex-Titan Quest dev (also a great ARPG), with a lot of offering in terms of very good graphics, multi-class characters and a lot of depth in gameplay.

Even though Grim Dawn looks like a classic Diablo clone, it is actually a lot more than that, because of the several reasons: the world is much larger; you have an ability to create a balance in the world between the factions (if one faction likes what you're doing, you can buy cheaper stuff from the merchants etc.); and dynamic weather - which is an awesome visual feature.

There are areas that could be somewhat improved, like combat animations and an ability to move the inventory around the screen, or at least to choose a position of the inventory in the GUI.

To sum it up, a very good ARPG offering.

Super good action-RPG. Played it mostly years ago after Diablo 3 finally made action-RPGs click for me. And this is rightly considered the successor to Diablo 2. But that doesn't do it justice. It's just a super good and fun game, atmospheric and supremely playable.

great gameplay with tons of build variety and solid combat. story kinda dull, but the freedom to mess around with different setups kept it fun.
good ride overall

Running around the map, messing with the mobs, collecting weapons and items, leveling character, choosing skills that suitable with my playstyle, then fighting against a boss, then continue run around the map... and repeat, but wait, this really made me addicted. The story is interested as well. Good game to spend time in.

The true diablo 3 !!! Dark atmosphere in a ruined world, with an amazing soundtrack. The RPG system in very deep and allows for a ridiculous amount of options. The late game has lot to offer, more or less everything you look for in a game like this.

A brilliant hack n slash / loot hoarder that outshines diablo in every way.

Pros:
Amazing character customization
Engrossing story
Challenging combat (with varying difficulty)
Interesting attack/spell animations
Co-op is available (I prefer solo personally in this game)

Cons:
graphics and the isometric angle didn't age the best over the years
customization may feel overwhelming for some

Don't listen to anyone that says there is only 'one right way' to build a class. The forums are filled with dozens and dozens of viable builds for each class. and the dualclass mechanic makes the combinations very interesting.

I do wish the game's graphics were updated, and for whatever reason, I'm not the biggest fan of the camera angle. but otherwise, the game is great.

I've been playing this game on and off since Alpha, when all you had was this little area outside Devil's Crossing (first town/settlement/whatever-fits-best) to run around and slay beaties in. I remember when I first heard that the guy who had worked on Titan Quest all those years ago, would be making an ARPG with an updated version of that engine and I was immediately on-board and had purchased an advanced copy from a link on their forums before there ever was an Alpha to play. I saved the code until it was available to play on Steam. As soon as I heard I could use it, I did. From Alpha to Beta, Beta to Full Release, I've been pleased with this game every step of the way.

Coming from someone who played Titan Quest and Immortal Throne all those years ago (and I still have the installation discs), this game was very easy for me to get into. Especially since I was used to the two-class system. To me, Grim Dawn takes everything that was great about Titan Quest and takes it up a notch. Single Player or Multiplayer, no matter. Great game. I'd probably even go as far as to say, that this is the best ARPG I've ever played. And still playing it.

This is the most underrated game of all time. It supports online multiplayer while single player is offline. It looks and feels good, similar to PoE, but you can rotate the camera 360 degrees. You get a lot of lore from reading notes, The skill system is similar to D2 in that each class has its own skills, but starting at level 10, you can pick a 2nd class to train skills in and there are additional passives from a Devotion system. Best of all, you can respec your points any time. It has a day/night cycle and a weather system. There's all kinds of loot. Combat is pretty satisfying. Damage applies to individual body parts.

Its a Diablo clone. Sad that I even bothered to Kickstart the game, as I thought it would bring something a little different to the genre. Maybe innovate somehow.

It utterly fails to do this.

Not only would I not recommend it. I would say that, for those who are somehow still not tired of this genre, Path of Exile is a better game.
Classic gameplay, deep character building, and a very beautiful/atmospheric world. If you ever enjoyed playing diablo or titan quest, you'll love this game.

Though this game is still in early access at the moment, you already get a huge amount of content for your money.

If you like dark fantasy and old school Hack & Slash games like Diablo I and II, Darkstone, Sacred or Dugeon Siege, this is definitely a must have. Furthermore, you get the incredibly flexible skill tree and leveling system from Titan Quest, which make the game even deeper, with, even at its early access stage, huge replayability. In addition to that, there's also an interesting crafting system.The grim atmosphere is well rendered with realistic graphics, which recalls of Diablo II style. This is much more than a promising game, this is already, in my opinion, a great game. Get it now, when it's cheap :D

Love this game! One of the best out there, as far as my opinion goes. There are SO many builds possible, and each one offers a different play style. You can burn through it or take your time and hit every detail, it is all good stuff!

If you're an ARPG'er than I would buy this game. This game is going to be a hit when development is finished.. I've been playing for a while and I'm a Lvl 12 soilder and this game ROCKS!!!!!!! I'm looking forward to the finished product and the expansions!!! For a small development team they do an awesome job with the builds.

After 3 years still one of the best RPGs out there.

Solid meta, solid mechanics, solid combat and solid performance. While waiting for that next "Diablo 2" this is a perfect game to wait with. Multiple expansions so far, all of which are well priced and add a wealth of new items and areas to explore.
If you love the Necromancer class with pets this is a fun build. Go full skeletons and Blight pet. All you have to do is walk around and your pets destroy everything.

A nice twist on the typical Diablo-style game, with multiclassing. If you enjoyed Diablo/Diablo 2 but want something with just a bit of a twist, this is worth playing. I also appreciate how the world is hand crafted rather than the random maps you get in many of the games in this genre. It gives the world more of a natural feeling. The lore is also pretty special in this game. The first Diablo-like game in a while where I actually gave a damn about the story.

Lots of fun, I've played two acts of Diablo and I can say that I prefer GD quite a bit. The combat and character development is a lot more in depth and have more permanency than Diablo's skill tree without being too unforgiving with bad builds. The game is better for casual play than both POE and D3 as POE is too grindy to play casually without online interactions and D3 is focused on paragon levlling. There isn't much of an endgame as far as I can see apart from maybe the crucible. Main focus here is definetely the levelling experience. Would definetely recommend for ARPG fans who want something a bit less time consuming and more fun and in depth than D3

3.6k hours into the game, but sadly the newest patch has gone down the lazy route of making dodge/roll mechanics a core gameplay feature. There are an incredible number of one-shot mechanics from poorly tuned bosses, and it feels like playtesting was done by the 0.01% of sweatlords using ultra-specific builds and gearing.

There are definitely some good changes, but fundamentally the core game design no longer feels like the Grim Dawn we knew and loved. Instead of building on what made the game great, it feels like it's chasing a completely different style of ARPG.

A fun Diablo-like, Grim Dawn hit all my buttons for a game like this. Combat is quick and punchy, most enemies don't feel bullet spongey so it feels good mowing them down. The game gives you a lot of freedoms with builds, I was a Pyromancer that fought with my gun that shot exploding elemental shells and my minion buddies. Atmosphere is good and the level design is fresh and dungeons are just the right length. I admit I kind of ignored most of the lore because I don't expect good writing in Diablo-likes but it seemed serviceable. I don't necessarily feel like replaying it anytime soon because of my backlog and having experienced some of the post-game bosses they just seem super grognardy, but I'll gladly go in Day 1 for any future expansion.

Easily one of the best arpgs i'v played. Great customization and itemization, Great setting in my opinion and its only improved so far. Feels like a game devs were passionate about making. I give it a 9/10 very solid game indeed.

Great game, pretty addictive ;)
reminds me of Champions of Norrath and Back to Arms, two of my favourite games back in PS2 days

One of the best hack and slash games that I have ever played, for real. I've tried a ton and this is the first that has really snagged my attention for this amount of time.
Give it a go.

cool game, i like the class combos and talent trees the most. alot of games nowadays seem to lack indepth character versatility in class and builds.
If you liked Diablo 1-2, hated Diablo 3, and you thought Path of Exile was great but just didnt have the same grimdark, demonic kinda feel as Diablo, this is definately a game for you

How amazing. Just buyed this to fill the gap until i got something i am waiting. And now i cant stop, even convince a friend to restart playing. Even if i only finished the normal mode now, i am very thrilled with the gaming experience. There are also enough ressources on the web to get started with it.
Sure, like many others i have a heavy past with DIablo 3 and 2 and even the first one. And what can i say - if you liked this, you probably will enjoy Grim Dawn.
The networking is maybe one of the problems you run into, it is a peer to peer networking, so no servers hosted on their site, be aware. Sometimes itgoes pretty smooth and sometimes it screwes up, be careful and valuate how important this aspect of the game is for you. If you are looking more for a single player experience with sporadic multiplayer games - go ahead.

Same amazing people who made titan quest are back with a very well executed game.

1. Bloody and large battles
2. Great music that fits perfectly to the enviorment
3. Hundreds of hours of gameplay even after completing the story
4. Still adding great content

I recommend greatly to anyone who has a childhood of titan quest like me or like gore action RPG's.

Beware, the store page of this game claims Full Controller Support and a Playable rating.

This is a lie.

This Game has partially working controller support at best.
This game was not made for controllers in mind.
The developers hacked a barely functioning alpha version into the game a couple of years after release and never iterated on it.
Crate Entertainment is clearly not interested in controller users. This is completely legitimate, it is their business decision.

What is not acceptable is the plainly wrong 'Full Controller Support' tag here on Steam by Valve and the 'Playable' rating that goes along with it.

You will not be able to play this game on the Steam Deck (unless you connect an external mouse/keyboard).

The Playable rating is undeserved and it should be downgraded Unsupported and the 'Full Controller Support' should be downgraded to 'Partial Controller Support'.

I enjoy this game a lot. The classes are fun to play with and include secondary class options to mix and match. I ended up playing Warlord (Oathkeeper/Soldier) with friends and Witch Hunter (Night Blade/Occultist) solo, and both are interesting mixes.

The only con is that multiplayer is still *incredibly* buggy. Frequently when playing with friends one or more of us can't loot items (only the host seems immune to this), and we've missed out on epic and legendary items because of it. It's a well documented bug and I'm a bit disappointed it's never been patched. Other than that extremely annoying bug, well done.

I've been playing quite a bit of ARPG lately. Path of Exile II, Diablo 4, Last Epoch, Titan Quest II... and now I came back to the classic.

Grim Dawn is heads and shoulders above the rest. Only TQ II gets even close. The graphics are becoming quite dated, but a texture mod helps with that quite a bit.

The gameplay is solid. Builds are meaningful. The atmosphere is gloriously dark and fighting visceral. Everything feels meaningful and crafted, not generated by an algorithm to make it longer and "more engaging". No damn microtransactions, live events or other modern idiocy.

This is ARPG at it's finest, even in 2025.
The new expansion saw my play time double, essentially perfect game, easily my fav in this entire genre, build depth and variety is incredible

This game is an evolution of Titan Quest. The most important improvement is the *feel* to the combat. It's hard to pinpoint, but there was just something off with Titan Quest combat. Attacks and spells did not feel impactful, muted sound effects, etc. By contract, Grim Dawn combat is very fluid and satisfying.

It also continues the excellent system of dual class selection with some expansions like the constellation and more build variety within a class.

Unfortunately, it is also a big step back in terms of the world design and story. Colors are a lot more muted and the world / dungeons feels much more same-y compared to TQ. It feels like it is more influenced by D2 grimdark style. The worldbuilding however is simply not as good as, say, Path of Exile, or even Diablo 2 in my opinion.

In the end, I would recommend to pick this up during the sale. If you were a fan of Titan Quest this is a no brainer. Highly recommended for most arpg fans as well.

If you like ARPGs definitely get this one. Also be sure to complete it on Veteran at least once, drops are much better in it. That being said, do try Normal when you want to test out a character build because once you chose your classes for a character they can't be changed. (You can still change how you allocate skill points in those classes though, but not mastery points those are fixed as well)

Pros

Dual class system makes each character play differently.
A big world to explore and secrets to find
Different factions, whose quests unlock as you increase your reputation with them.
Good crafting system, and some nice abilities and passive bonuses can be imparted to your gear from components you find.
Notes scattered around the world are well written.

Cons

No option to hide quest from being displayed at all times. (There's a toggle to hide the entire panel but no option to hide individual ones) Also quests once taken can't be abandoned.

I have returned to this game every time a new expansion got released to have some fun, kill some mobs, get some loot, happy me. This time however the fun is mediocre at best. The game now feels it shifted towards long time players who grinded out all the gear. This wouldn't be much of a problem if it was only on higher difficulty levels but it's also apparent in normal difficulty, the one were you start your journey when you're a new player. 

The bosses nowadays either wreck you because you don't have the proper resistance/defence, or if you do it takes ages because the health pools have had a massive increase. For a new player it will be hard to get these in the right window because you don't have the items to offset these requirements. I don't understand why they went this route on a starting difficulty. You force the players to already pay attention without them having the knowledge. 

That's why I can't recommend this game to new players.

This game presents a very unique way to customize your character with the two class system. Gear upgrades actually impact your play-style in drastic ways. The graphics are a bit dated but easily overlooked. Unlike most arpgs, this game has a story that is surprisingly dark. The expansions just build on to what the base game was already doing well, with forgotten gods being a personal favorite because it adds an infinite dungeon. Overall, great game that feels complete. Also, no cash shop, so that's always a plus.

Lovers of PoE, Diablo and Baldur's Gate, get ready for a hell of an adventure with some key improvements and differences from the games you adore/

A lot has been said so I'll just say I like the inventory a bit better, you can multi-class very early and easily, and the unique levelling system gives you points you can dump into skills or into the level of your class, your choice. So you can be level 1 in your job with just one OP level 20 skill so you can one-shot things with in the early game. And if you regret it, refunding is cheap.

That's all, have fun!

I would like to report a bug.

In the quest "Lumber for the Legion," I cleared out the mill first before activating the quest. However, the game does not recognize that I have already cleared the mill, similar to other quests where you have the option of claiming your reward immediately. Now, I went back to the mill again, but the enemies do not respawn anymore for me to claim the quest. I might need to restart the instance and repeat.

Year after year this ARPG continues to impress. Highly recommend picking this game up along with the DLC if you are a fan of PoE or Diablo. With all the love the devs give this game it deserves the high praise. One of the few games I love coming back to every so often and with tons of achievements to hunt for and hundreds of builds to try out. The community is very active with builds, mods and quest guides!`

I loved immortal empires.
Immortal empires is what made me mod Torchlight 2.
When Grim dawn came out I had just generally finished modding Torchlight 2 for over 2000+ hours, and I was tired of ARPGS.
Finally my friends took interest into grimdawn.

I love the game, although I struggle with its facetank mechanics as the main way to survive, it is an amazingly well made game. I would recommend it to everyone.

Grim Dawn – The Hidden Gem of ARPGs
Hours Played: 73.3

Grim Dawn is one of the best ARPGs out there, blending deep character customization, satisfying combat, and a dark, immersive world. If you love games like Diablo 2, Path of Exile, or Titan Quest, this is a must-play.

The Good
✅ Dual-Class System – Mixing two classes creates endless build possibilities. Want a spell-slinging tank? A pet-based necromancer? Go for it.

✅ Deep & Rewarding Loot System – Tons of unique items, legendary gear, and build-defining weapons keep the grind exciting.

✅ Engaging Combat – Smooth, impactful, and skill-based, making every fight feel rewarding.

✅ Dark & Gritty World – A Lovecraftian apocalypse mixed with steampunk and medieval fantasy—the atmosphere is amazing.

✅ Offline Play & Mods – No always-online nonsense. Play solo, co-op, or mod the game to your liking.

The Bad
❌ UI & Inventory Management Could Be Better – Sorting loot can be a bit clunky, though mods help.

❌ Endgame Can Feel Grind-Heavy – Reaching optimal gear takes time, and farming can become repetitive.

❌ Story is Decent but Not the Focus – While the lore is interesting, don’t expect a narrative masterpiece.

Final Verdict
With 73+ hours, I can say Grim Dawn is one of the most underrated ARPGs. If you want deep character builds, satisfying loot, and tons of replayability, this game delivers in spades.

Rating: 9/10 – A hardcore ARPG fan’s dream. ⚔️🔥

Great game. Lots of options for the kind of character you want to play. Plays well on low power systems as well as ones with bigger, faster graphics cards/cpus, etc. It's fun, exciting, frustrating game and you will die (in my case, multiple times!) but gets you back into the game to continue the fight. Would recommend it for anyone interested in games that are fun and challenging.
Played for about 8 hours so far and not even close to finishing the game, very content rich, enjoyable combat and skill progression.

A very good hack and slash ARPG since Titan Quest, this game feel like a revival of my old RPG experience, I highly recommended it. The game itself feel completed already but the AOM expansion make it 150%. I can't wait for the FG expansion.

Have played this game here and there across the past decade now, but definitely getting more and more into recently. The updates they have done for the game have provided so much QoL, and the new QoL teased elevates the game even further into a purely smooth experience.
Each class combo offers a different tactic and playstyle combo, with each combo itself letting you diversify deeper with different weapon types (melee and ranged), and then ON TOP of all that comes the devotion system to let you add more nuance to your own build and disintegrate whatever is in front of you in a new cruel and unusual manner.
If you've played Titan Quest in the past, or old ARPGs, this will likely be right up your alley, especially if you like yourself some eldritch horror.

If you're used to games like Diablo and such be sure to have the difficulty set to Veteran though, as it can become a little too easy otherwise in my opinion.
The only thing this game is bad at is the fact that you need to beat the game 3 times to get to the end game content which can get repetative but other that that it's the best arpg out there.

tldr.text: Very Positive (95%): players praise the story, characters and combat.
The most common complaint is about the story and characters, followed by the price and bugs and crashes.

details.text: Recent reviews complain far less about bugs and crashes, and about the story and characters, than reviews did overall.
New players are much less positive than veterans, and one reviewer blames a "boring grind" that comes after the early hours.
